findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "estimate_dog_insurance_cost" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "estimate_dog_insurance_cost" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "match_dog_breeds" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: match_dog_breeds, assess_breed_fit, create_test_drive_plan, review_test_drive · Public sink: match_dog_breeds, find_similar_breeds.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: match_dog_breeds, assess_breed_fit, create_test_drive_plan, review_test_drive · Public sink: match_dog_breeds, find_similar_breeds

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_breeds" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
